[tool: fetch_url https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-05-anthropic-ai-rd-acceleration-assessment/#interview-quotes, part 1/4: headline] result:
METR, 'Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026' (Nov 5, 2026). Headline: Anthropic is likely improving on well-specified tasks at about 2x its March 2024 to October 2025 rate; METR would not be surprised if the true figure were 1.3x or 3x. Trend fit on AECI: 1.9x [1.5-2.8] since October 2025, roughly two years of historical progress over the last year. Robustness analyses find acceleration rates between 1.1x and 2.9x. METR guesses that a majority (perhaps ≈80%) of the current acceleration is due to AI. Staff self-reported uplift is ≈12x for the most capable internal model. METR found no convincing bottlenecks for the next 12 months. Interview section: 28 quotes from 11 researchers (A-L, no I), each classified by METR as Yes, Leans yes, Borderline, Unclear or No. Quotes over 125 characters are cut with '…'.

[tool: fetch_url https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-05-anthropic-ai-rd-acceleration-assessment/#interview-quotes, part 2/4: quotes A-B] result:
Researcher A (METR classification: Yes)
  1. "Could definitely endorse a greater than 2X speedup" [METR interview notes]
  2. "My inside view is by far the largest effect is model acceleration" [METR interview notes]
  3. "The AI acceleration is larger than all the other effects." [METR interview notes]
  4. "Now only bottlenecked on ideas & compute, no longer bottlenecked on code." [METR interview notes]
  5. "I would definitely endorse >2 years of progress in 1 year and I don't think 4 is crazy." [METR interview notes]
  6. "I think there's some truth to the 'we just started trying harder' story, but IMO the bulk of the effect is recent models." [METR interview notes]
  7. "Like 80% reduction in time between idea and experiment, other 20% some mix of making fewer mistakes and being able to measure…" [METR interview notes]
  8. "I think there was a medium bump when it was good enough to code at all and a big bump with Opus-4.5/Opus 4.6 and…" [Anthropic interview notes]
Researcher B (METR classification: Yes)
  1. "It is hard to see how I am not being 3x more productive. I feel like I have postdocs and grad students, and…" [METR interview notes]

[tool: fetch_url https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-05-anthropic-ai-rd-acceleration-assessment/#interview-quotes, part 3/4: quotes C-G] result:
Researcher C (METR classification: Leans yes)
  1. "this is probably the biggest factor imo. When people present experiments, they most often just point to an [agent scaffold] thread." [Anthropic interview notes]
  2. "I think CC was already good enough before mythos-preview to implement most ideas around Opus 4.5" [Anthropic interview notes]
Researcher D (METR classification: Leans yes)
  1. "It is just much easier to [perform] lots of [redacted] experiments that would have taken days. People don't try [redacted]…" [Anthropic interview notes]
  2. "I personally think this is a large lift and has led to me trying far more ideas." [Anthropic interview notes]
  3. "On a linear scale, ~0 uplift pre Opus 4.6/Opus-4.5, ~some uplift that was small with them, large uplift with mythos-preview + [agent-scaffold]…" [Anthropic interview notes]
Researcher E (METR classification: Leans yes)
  1. "I do genuinely think Claude (claude code, [agent-scaffold]) has been fairly significant. I've seen us discovering…" [Anthropic interview notes]
  2. "A lot of [redacted] research work is just implementation, babysitting, etc. Opus-4.5 in claude code is already pretty helpful…" [Anthropic interview notes]
Researcher F (METR classification: Borderline)
  1. "The slope change is 50-80% Claude" [Anthropic interview notes]
  2. "Change is especially notable for this manager, who can de-risk ideas with Claude enough to get someone else excited, and would not…" [Anthropic interview notes (paraphrase)]
Researcher G (METR classification: Unclear)
  1. "Inflection point matches his vibes as to what's been happening. Two biggest contributors here are Claude automation…" [Anthropic interview notes (paraphrase)]
  2. "Claude lets researchers try many things quickly, most of which won't work. …" [Anthropic interview notes]

[tool: fetch_url https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-05-anthropic-ai-rd-acceleration-assessment/#interview-quotes, part 4/4: quotes H-L] result:
Researcher H (METR classification: Unclear)
  1. "I think it's true [that] we're now trying a lot more experiments at the same time because of claudification." [Anthropic interview notes]
Researcher J (METR classification: Unclear)
  1. "Before Opus-4.5 -> Claude not useful for autonomous code / Opus-4.5 -> first time useful for autonomous code / …" [Anthropic interview notes]
Researcher K (METR classification: No)
  1. "IMO [hiring is] probably the biggest reason …" [Anthropic interview notes]
Researcher L (METR classification: No)
  1. "Guesses 15-20% is due to AI. Don't believe in self-reported productivity increase." [METR interview notes]
  2. "My favored interpretation: [redacted non-AI factor]" [METR interview notes]
  3. "(1) opus45 couldn't write code; (2) opus46 could write a little; (3) Mythos Preview a sharp inflection; (4) Model 2 is…" [METR interview notes]
  4. "definitely the case that we're accelerated by claude .. Even though this rate of progress by end of year will be even faster…" [METR interview notes]
  5. "One impact is SWE acceleration, which is extremely substantial. We're definitely benefiting from that differentially…" [METR interview notes]
